title: Fix the order factory: defaults, shallow copies, aliasing
problem: new_order() builds order dicts for a shop, but orders leak into each other: one customer's pen shows up in another's order, notes appear on every order, and the caller's own list changes. Run pytest, draw the labels for a failing test, and fix new_order without changing the tests or the two helpers.
requirements: Each order owns its own 'items' and 'notes' lists, never shared with other orders, BLANK_ORDER or the caller
Calling new_order without items gives an empty items list
Don't modify test_orders.py, add_item or add_note
contract: new_order(order_id: int, items: list[str] | None = None) -> dict
expectedBehavior: a = new_order(1); b = new_order(2); add_item(a, 'pen') leaves b['items'] == []; mine = ['pen']; add_item(new_order(3, mine), 'ink') leaves mine == ['pen']
edgeCases: An empty list passed by the caller
hints: Conceptual: there are three places where an order ends up pointing at a list that something else also points at: the default argument, the caller's argument and the template. Draw the labels for test_default_orders_do_not_share_items and test_notes_are_not_shared_between_orders.

Specific: the default [] is created once, when def runs (L04 section 5). BLANK_ORDER.copy() is shallow, so its inner lists are shared (section 2). order['items'] = items stores the caller's list itself.
Implementation: make the default None and only use items when it is not None; copy the template with copy.deepcopy; store list(items) instead of items.
evaluation: All six tests pass, also when each is run alone
The tests and the two helpers are unchanged
No mutable default argument remains; the template and the caller's list are copied, not aliased
